Release notesKTPH000
What changed in the current release. The version this guide was built for is shown in the footer.
Terminal loggingKTPH000

KTPH002Connection logging was rebuilt to actually be reliableKTPH003 — KTPH004terminal loggingKTPH005 previously wrote every connection to one fixed path (so two connections open at once interleaved into the same file), had no compression, and rotated by KTPH006deletingKTPH007 the file at the size limit. Files are now named KTPH000, a fresh one starts every day (optional) and whenever the size limit is hit, nothing is ever overwritten or deleted by rotation, and each closed file is gzip-compressed. Old archives are swept by the date encoded in their name once the retention period (default 30 days, KTPH001 keeps everything) expires, and only korTTY's own log files are ever touched, so it is safe to point the setting at a folder used for other things too.

KTPH000The terminal log is now redactedKTPH001 — captured lines pass through the same redaction as the session journal before anything is written: the connection's own stored password and any replacement rules an organization's policy defines. Log files, and a log folder korTTY created itself, are set to owner-only permissions where the filesystem supports it.

KTPH000Quick Connect gained a Terminal log sectionKTPH001 — configuring logging in the Connection Manager and then connecting from Quick Connect with a different authentication method previously dropped the setting silently; Quick Connect now carries its own folder, format and compression controls and applies them to the session it opens.

KTPH000Fixed: XML and JSON logs had two document roots and never parsedKTPH001, rotation wrote the closing footer twice, up to 10,000 queued lines from just before a disconnect could be silently dropped, and output was split on line endings in a way that destroyed indentation and turned every progress-bar frame into its own log entry. All four are fixed.
Session journal: filtered export, named markers, page appearance and screenshot editingKTPH000

KTPH003Exports can now be narrowed downKTPH004 — KTPH005Exporting only part of a journalKTPH006 accepts any number of time windows (an entry only needs to fall into one of them), a topic filter as literal text, a regular expression, or handed to the AI to select by meaning, and a marker filter (all entries, only marked ones, or specific markers). Times are parsed leniently (KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002 all work) and widened by an adjustable tolerance (± 5 minutes by default), so an approximate window still catches the entry that actually straddles it. A filtered HTML bundle is rebuilt rather than copied — trimmed capture log, only the referenced screenshots — so a shared export cannot leak the rest of the session; every filtered PDF, Markdown file and bundle carries a banner naming the range so nobody mistakes it for the complete journal.

KTPH000Markers are no longer a fixed four-value listKTPH001 — beyond the built-ins (None, Info, Important, Error) you can now define KTPH002custom markersKTPH003, give each one a name and colour, and map it to one of the built-ins for older journals and for the error/important counts. Optional rules apply a marker automatically as entries are captured, matching a literal term or a regular expression against the entry's title, summary, note and excerpts, with precedence KTPH004your own choice KTPH006 a rule KTPH007 the AI's suggestionKTPH005 — a rule never overwrites a marker you set by hand.

KTPH000The journal page has adjustable KTPH001appearanceKTPH002KTPH003 — a colour scheme (six fixed palettes, the page's automatic light/dark pair, or a scheme derived live from your terminal's own colours), a text font and a monospace font, chosen from a toolbar popover and remembered for every journal korTTY renders afterwards.

KTPH001Screenshots can be KTPH002annotatedKTPH003KTPH004 — pen, box, an "Unreadable" tool that coarsens a region into blocks, and text labels, plus a note field, reachable by right-clicking a screenshot. Marks are stored as data and stay re-editable; the untouched capture is kept locally as KTPH000 and is never included in an export. This obscures a value in the rendered page, it does not redact it — use Search KTPH005 replace or a policy redaction rule to remove something from a journal for good.

KTPH000Selecting a time range got easierKTPH001 — inside korTTY the viewer's timeline can be switched into range-selection mode: click a first and a last entry to highlight the span between them and hand it straight to the export dialog, or collect several windows before exporting. The same selection is available from the edit-mode entry table via right-click.
KTPH000You can edit a journal title directly on its pageKTPH001, and a header button jumps from one marked entry to the next.
Live journal side panelKTPH000

KTPH003A running journal can now be watched — and worked with — in real timeKTPH004 — KTPH005View → Live JournalKTPH006 (KTPH007KTPH000KTPH008+KTPH009KTPH001KTPH010+KTPH011KTPH002KTPH012) docks the KTPH013live journal panelKTPH014 to the left or right of the terminal. It shows the journal's KTPH015full pageKTPH016, the same one the viewer renders: the timeline with AI summaries, notes and screenshots, plus an on-demand KTPH017Live LogKTPH018 view streaming the capture log as it is written — output lines, your typed commands, notes and screenshot markers. New timeline cards and edits appear moments after they happen without losing your scroll position; the live log starts hidden, a header button shows or hides it, its height is drag-adjustable and remembered, scrolling it up pauses following and scrolling back down resumes it, and a header menu switches the page between light and dark. Terminal AI-agent replies are captured into the journal's log, and every agent run writes its own KTPH019AI agentKTPH020 timeline card — prompt as title, final answer as body — the moment it completes. Because it is the real page, its actions work right in the panel: right-click a screenshot to annotate it (the edited picture appears on save), pick markers, search, and open entry log excerpts; the header adds KTPH021NoteKTPH022, KTPH023ScreenshotKTPH024 and KTPH025Open ViewerKTPH026. The panel shows the journal of the current tab and only switches on a tab change when the new tab also has a running journal — otherwise it keeps the journal it shows, and a stopped journal or closed tab leaves the page in place with a badge. Side and width are remembered across restarts. Everything shown has already passed the journal's password protection, so suppressed input and redacted secrets never appear.

KTPH002The interface font size can now be set, and optionally follows the displayKTPH003 — a high-resolution monitor left korTTY's own text, the menu bar most of all, uncomfortably small, because every size in the interface was fixed in pixels. KTPH004UI font sizeKTPH005 on the Appearance tab now scales the whole interface between 80 % and 160 %: the menu bar and its dropdowns, dialogs, labels, buttons, tab titles, the dashboard, the file browser and the status bar. It applies the moment you save, to windows that are already open as well as new ones, and the main window's first-launch size and any remembered dialog sizes are re-measured to match. KTPH006Match display resolutionKTPH007 derives the value from the primary display's logical resolution instead, which leaves a Retina panel at 100 % — macOS has already scaled it — and raises a 4K display running at 100 % operating-system scaling to 125 %. Surfaces that already have their own size control are deliberately left alone, so nothing gains two competing settings: terminal sessions keep the Font tab and the zoom shortcuts, the editor keeps the Editor tab, and the AI chat, plan and activity panels keep their KTPH000 / KTPH001 buttons. Two parts stay fixed at every setting: the macOS application menu, which the operating system draws, and the AI swarm status strip, whose labels are painted onto a canvas alongside hand-computed positions.

KTPH009The manual has its own text sizeKTPH010 — the manual window (KTPH011Help → ManualKTPH012, KTPH013KTPH002KTPH014) now has three buttons at its top left: KTPH000, the current percentage, and KTPH001. Clicking the percentage resets it to 100 %. The shortcuts KTPH015KTPH003KTPH016+KTPH017KTPH004KTPH018, KTPH019KTPH005KTPH020+KTPH021KTPH006KTPH022 and KTPH023KTPH007KTPH024+KTPH025KTPH008KTPH026 do the same. The setting scales the whole page between 70 % and 250 %, applies to the AI search answers beside it, and survives both navigation and a restart. It is separate from the interface setting above, because the manual is a document you read at length, and the size that suits a dialog rarely suits a page of prose. See KTPH027Manual text sizeKTPH028.
Snippet editorKTPH000

KTPH002The change preview can be read one finding at a timeKTPH003 — a KTPH004HighlightKTPH005 picker below the diff narrows the review to a single improvement or hardening id (KTPH000, KTPH001, …): only that finding's places keep their marker and get a coloured line background, every other changed block is muted to a neutral tint, the window scrolls to the first place, and the explanation cards below shrink to match. KTPH006◀KTPH007 / KTPH008▶KTPH009 beside the picker walk the list one finding at a time, wrapping at the ends, so a report can be worked through without opening the dropdown for every step. KTPH010All changesKTPH011 restores the full colouring. Muted blocks stay visible and keep their change markers, so this approval step never makes a real change invisible. The summary at the top now scrolls in its own pane above a draggable divider, so a staged apply's paragraph-per-stage summary no longer pushes the code out of view. The window also remembers the size and position you gave it, and the divider once you move it yourself.

KTPH001Fixed incomplete Full code analysis replacementsKTPH002 — every KTPH003Apply selectedKTPH004 stage asks for one full rewritten script, explicitly requires every unchanged section to be copied, and refuses omission markers such as KTPH000 before another stage or the review window can use the result.

KTPH000Fixed the snippet Text language scopeKTPH001 — every AI action that returns code now requires all existing and new comments, every displayed message, every log message, and every help message in that returned scope to use the selected language. A Full code analysis replacement applies the rule to the entire script while its report and diagram labels continue to follow the interface language.

KTPH000Reduced Full code analysis prompt and skill bloatKTPH001 — analysis and diagram requests now send one line-numbered script copy instead of repeating the same source as raw and numbered text. An explicit snippet-skill selection is used as an allowlist instead of being combined with another automatic relevance pass, and ordinary automatic matching keeps only its strongest candidates.

KTPH002Optimized and hardened Mermaid diagram generationKTPH003 — diagram-only requests no longer carry configurable coding Skills, knowledge-store excerpts, a linear example that could anchor the model, or repeated copies of the Mermaid contract. A compact immutable Mermaid action skill is now always included instead: it asks for grouped runtime behavior, localized KTPH004yesKTPH005/KTPH006noKTPH007 branches and loop exits, connected start-to-stop paths and exact source ranges. Fresh AI results with disconnected nodes, backward terminal paths, incomplete decisions, more than 12 action/decision nodes or incomplete source mappings are rejected and use the local fallback without an AI retry, while safe stored diagrams remain backward-compatible; built-in interface languages also get a local edge-label check. When the KTPH000 KTPH008ReasoningKTPH009 value is available and the profile has a fixed model selection, korTTY automatically uses it for the diagram request without changing the saved profile. An Auto profile is not overridden from previously discovered capabilities because its loaded model can change; an explicitly configured KTPH001 value still applies. OpenAI-compatible HTTP, LM Studio native, and embedded llama.cpp/MLX transports cap the response at 8,192 tokens, while Anthropic retains its separate provider cap. For embedded llama.cpp/MLX, korTTY does not repeat a response that is empty or contains only the model's reasoning; replacing or closing a pending diagram also cancels the superseded client request.

KTPH002Added output limits for code replacementsKTPH003 — A finite output limit now applies to Full code analysis, security-fix, hardening and assistant replacements over OpenAI-compatible HTTP, LM Studio native, and embedded llama.cpp/MLX. It scales from 32,768 to 65,536 tokens with the source size; Anthropic retains its separate provider cap. When korTTY applies selected Full code analysis improvements or security fixes, it automatically requests KTPH000 Reasoning only if that value is available and the profile has a fixed model selection. An Auto profile keeps its configured or provider-default Reasoning behavior unless KTPH001 was explicitly configured. This prevents binary on/off reasoning models from spending the complete replacement budget before emitting the script. A provider-reported or malformed truncated response — including a reasoning-only answer with empty visible content — is recorded and rejected with the localized output-limit status and cannot change the editor or trigger an AI retry. Very large full-script replacements can therefore be refused rather than partially applied.

KTPH006LM Studio reasoning-option detection was fixedKTPH007 — KTPH008Refresh reasoning optionsKTPH009 now prefers the model's exact native KTPH000 metadata. A binary KTPH001/KTPH002 model no longer shows the Minimal, Low, Medium, High, or Extra high levels as supported merely because LM Studio silently converts an unsupported value to KTPH003; an explicit KTPH004 request switches this feature off, while omitting the parameter uses the published provider default. A model that publishes no reasoning capability at all — a coder model, or a virtual model whose configuration overrides reasoning metadata to false — now offers only KTPH010DisabledKTPH011 instead of every level: LM Studio skips an unsupported request-time reasoning value with a log warning instead of rejecting the request, so the active probe mistook every level for supported and korTTY kept sending an explicit KTPH005. Levels detected by an earlier version are no longer trusted, since they may have come from that probe: HTTP and CLI profiles fall back to the conservative defaults for their model name until KTPH012Refresh reasoning optionsKTPH013 is pressed once more, so an affected profile stops sending the parameter without anyone having to know about the button. Nothing is deleted from the settings file, and profiles using an integrated model keep their detected levels.

KTPH003Fixed the Input hardening file-size guardKTPH004 — generated scripts now use KTPH000, check file metadata before reading any content, reject oversized files without reading them, and treat KTPH001 as an unlimited size. The size field now accepts KTPH002 accordingly.

KTPH000Audited every Hardening and Input hardening optionKTPH001 — leaving a classic option unselected no longer lets the same behaviour return through unconditional language-specific defaults, and each input sub-option now names only its own checks, helpers and exit-code cases. Global hardening selected in KTPH002Improve robustnessKTPH003 or KTPH004Custom improvementKTPH005 now rewrites the complete snippet so prologue and epilogue rules can actually be applied.

KTPH008Stopped partial hardening in Full code analysisKTPH009 — KTPH010Apply selectedKTPH011 assigns every selected classic and input-hardening rule a stable mandatory identifier, batches analysis items and dependencies into apply stages of at most three, processes the two hardening categories separately in batches of at most three mandatory requirements, and verifies the cumulative completed-identifier list without demanding one verbose change record per rule. Missing requirements reject the whole staged result, while explicit selected flags and guard literals such as KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002, KTPH003, KTPH004, KTPH005, KTPH006, and KTPH007 must be present in the final script.

KTPH000Made staged Apply selected requests survive a dropped connectionKTPH001 — a stage whose response stream is cut off mid-answer by the connection is now retried once automatically and reported as an interrupted connection, instead of aborting the whole apply and misreporting it as the output-token limit. Long-running chat requests (Full code analysis, security fixes, hardening, the assistant) now stream over OpenAI-compatible HTTP so a slow generation keeps bytes flowing and survives gateway idle timeouts; a MiniMax profile with reasoning turned off now also disables MiniMax's own "thinking" budget instead of silently spending it anyway.

KTPH001Fixed empty Full code analysis apply results from malformed local-model JSONKTPH002 — each stage now returns the complete script as a structured array with one source line per entry instead of one escape-sensitive JSON string. OpenAI-compatible requests enforce that shape and a conservative minimum line count through a strict JSON response schema, dropping the schema only when the endpoint explicitly rejects structured output. The compatibility parser still preserves source escapes such as KTPH000 where possible.

KTPH000Made Full code analysis apply progress visible and atomicKTPH001 — the analysis report now stays open while a narrow AI-processing companion window docks beside it. Separate progress bars for improvements and code hardening, elapsed time and provider-reported cumulative token usage sit above a complete checklist. Improvement and dependency rows show their colour-coded category icon directly after the item ID rather than reserving a narrow right-hand column for category and severity text; hardening requirements rely on the KTPH002Code hardeningKTPH003 section heading. Checklist descriptions are capped at three lines with an ellipsis while the complete text remains visible in the adjacent analysis report. The active batch is visible, every completed item receives a green checkmark and a failed or retried step remains identifiable. Each stage builds on the previous full script, but intermediate results remain hidden and are never applied on their own. A stage gets at most one visible repair attempt after either a short non-truncated fragment or a complete response that omits a mandatory identifier or required literal. Requirement repair starts from the complete returned script and names the unresolved identifiers; a second failure reports those identifiers and discards the sequence. Exactly one final review preview opens only after cumulative validation succeeds.

KTPH001A stage that undoes an earlier stage's hardening is now caught immediatelyKTPH002 — every KTPH003Apply selectedKTPH004 stage rewrites the whole script, so a later stage could silently drop work an earlier one had already delivered (for example the KTPH000 handling of a selected rule). Only the final validation noticed, after every stage had run and with no way to resume. Each stage is now also checked against the literals of the rules earlier stages delivered, so the offending stage fails right away, gets its one repair attempt naming exactly what to restore, and the run stays resumable if that attempt does not fix it.

KTPH000An interrupted Apply selected can now be resumed or partially appliedKTPH001 — when the staged run stops after at least one completed stage (an AI or connection failure, or the editor's cancel button), an KTPH002Apply interruptedKTPH003 prompt offers three ways out: continue the remaining stages from the point of interruption while keeping the completed work, review the completed stages' combined rewrite in the usual before/after preview and apply it from there, or discard everything as before. Closing the analysis window or the snippet editor mid-run still discards silently, and a run that aborts before its first completed stage keeps the previous behavior.

KTPH000Made unavailable input guards explicitKTPH001 — Input hardening is now disabled, and yields no effective saved configuration, for YAML/YML/Ansible targets in workflow, swarm, improvement and Full code analysis dialogs instead of accepting a selection that would later be ignored.

KTPH000Fixed an Auto AI Complete popup during Full code analysisKTPH001 — starting the analysis now discards a pending completion timer and closes any visible ghost suggestion instead of allowing a stale completion popup to appear over the analysis flow.
